blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights the parallels between the design principles of the Internet and the emerging need for interoperable blockchain systems. The paper by Hardjono et al. argues that for blockchain technology to become a fundamental component of global commerce, it must adopt core Internet-like principles such as survivability, support for multiple service types, and accommodation of diverse systems. The authors propose a design philosophy for blockchains that emphasizes interoperability at both the mechanical (transaction execution) and value (semantic compatibility) levels. Key insights include the need for survivability in transactions, the role of gateways in mediating cross-chain transactions, and the separation of technical trust from legal trust frameworks. The MIT Tradecoin project is cited as a practical example of this approach.
paper_title: Towards a design philosophy for interoperable blockchain systems
paper_abstract: In this paper we discuss a design philosophy for interoperable blockchain systems, using the design philosophy of the Internet architecture as the basis to identify key design principles. Several interoperability challenges are discussed in the context of cross-domain transactions. We illustrate how these principles are informing the interoperability architecture of the MIT Tradecoin system. 1 Contents
